lead: The method of sections finds a few member forces in a truss without solving every joint. You draw an imaginary cut through the truss, take one part as a free body, and apply three equilibrium equations to that part. It exists because joint-by-joint work is wasteful when a design check asks only for one or two members. In practice it is used to check the chord or diagonal near a heavy load, to size a member in a roof truss, or to verify software output for a bridge panel.
prereq: You need Chapter 3.1 for tension and compression signs, and Unit 2 for free body diagrams, supports and equilibrium of rigid bodies.

sections.h3: The cut and the free body

blocks.text: The method of joints in Chapter 3.1 starts at one joint and works across the whole truss. The method of sections starts with a cut. A section is an imaginary line drawn through members. It separates the truss into two parts. Each part is then a rigid body in equilibrium under its own external forces and the cut member forces.

Use a section when only a few member forces are wanted. A single section normally cuts at most three members with unknown forces. Three equations are available for a planar body: ΣF<sub>x</sub> = 0, ΣF<sub>y</sub> = 0 and ΣM = 0. If the cut meets four unknown members, the three equations cannot find all four. If one of those four is already known or is a zero-force member, the cut is still usable.

A cut member force is drawn as tension unless you already expect compression. Tension pulls away from the cut face on the chosen part. Compression pushes toward the cut face. After solving, a plus sign means tension and a minus sign means compression. Some syllabi call this the method of sections.

blocks.where: ΣF<sub>x</sub> and ΣF<sub>y</sub> are sums of force components on the chosen part; ΣM<sub>P</sub> is the sum of moments about any point P in the plane; P need not lie on the part.

sections.h3: Choose the cut and the moment point

blocks.text: The cut should pass through the member you want. It should also pass through no more than two other unknown members. Pick the part with fewer loads and reactions; that part gives shorter equations.

items: Find the support reactions from the whole truss if the chosen part contains a support.
Draw the section through the wanted member. Take one part as the free body.
Show every external load and support reaction that acts on that part. Leave out forces that act only on the other part.
Draw each cut member force as tension, pulling away from the cut face.
For a moment equation, choose P where the lines of action of two unknown cut members meet. Those two then have zero moment about P.
If two unknown cut members are parallel, use ΣF in the direction perpendicular to them. Their components in that direction are zero.
Solve. A positive result is tension; a negative result is compression.

blocks.text: A moment point can be outside the free body. Equilibrium of a rigid body allows moments about any point in the plane. This is the trick that makes the method fast.

sections.h3: Check the answer at a joint

blocks.text: A section result is easy to check. Put the force back at a joint on the cut and test ΣF<sub>x</sub> = 0 and ΣF<sub>y</sub> = 0 there. Use the support reaction at that joint if it has one. The check catches a wrong sign, a missed reaction, or a wrong angle.

Keep units consistent. Member forces are in kN if loads are in kN; lengths may stay in metres because they cancel in the angle ratios. Write the sign and the word tension or compression in the final answer. A bare negative number is not enough in an exam.

A section does not have to be vertical. Any line that separates the truss into two parts works. The line may pass through several members, but only three unknown member forces can be handled by the three equations. In the worked example, a vertical section cuts EF, CE and BC, and the right part gives CE directly.

figure.caption: The dashed members BC, CE and EF are cut by a vertical section between the two panels. The right free body has only the roller reaction at C and the three cut forces, so CE follows from the vertical force sum.

spec.aria: A two-panel truss with A pin, C roller, a 10 kN downward load at E, and dashed cut members EF, CE and BC.

examples.question: For the truss A(0,0), B(2,0), C(4,0), D(0,3), E(2,3), F(4,3), members AB, BC, DE, EF, AD, BE, CF, AE and CE carry a 10 kN downward load at E. A is a pin and C is a roller. Use a vertical section cutting EF, CE and BC to find the force in CE. Check the result at joint C.
steps: Take moments about A for the whole truss. The 10 kN load at E is 2 m from A; the roller reaction C<sub>y</sub> is 4 m from A. ΣM<sub>A</sub> = 0 gives C<sub>y</sub> × 4 m − 10 kN × 2 m = 0, so C<sub>y</sub> = 5 kN upward. ΣF<sub>y</sub> = 0 gives A<sub>y</sub> = 5 kN upward.

Cut vertically between x = 2 m and x = 4 m. The cut members are EF, CE and BC. Take the right part C-F. On this part, the only external force is C<sub>y</sub> = 5 kN upward at C. The 10 kN load at E is on the left part, so it is not included.
Let T<sub>CE</sub> be tension in CE. At C it pulls toward E, in direction (−2, 3)/√13. EF and BC are horizontal, so they have no vertical component.
Sum vertical forces on the right part: 5 kN + T<sub>CE</sub>(3/√13) = 0. Hence T<sub>CE</sub> = −5√13/3 kN = −6.009 kN.
The negative sign means compression. The force in CE is 6.01 kN compression.
Check: take moments about E for the right part. ΣM<sub>E</sub> = 0 gives T<sub>BC</sub> × 3 m = 5 kN × 2 m, so T<sub>BC</sub> = 3.33 kN tension.
At joint C, BC pulls left with 3.33 kN. CE compression pushes down-right with components 3.33 kN right and 5 kN down. The roller reaction is 5 kN up. These balance in both directions.
examples.answer: CE = −6.01 kN; the member is in compression with magnitude 6.01 kN.
examples.check:
import math
load = 10.0
x_load = 2.0
span = 4.0
height = 3.0
Cy = load * x_load / span
CE = -Cy * math.sqrt(2.0**2 + height**2) / height
print(f"{CE:.2f}")

traps: Cutting four unknown members and trying to solve with three equations. A section normally handles at most three unknown member forces.
Leaving out a support reaction on the chosen part. If the part contains C, the roller reaction at C belongs in the equations.
Using the whole truss after the cut. Each equation must use only forces on the chosen free body.
Reporting −6.01 kN without saying compression. In exams, give magnitude and the word tension or compression.
Taking moments about a point that lies on all unknown lines. If two unknowns pass through the point, the equation cannot find them.

quiz.q: A single section normally cuts how many unknown member forces? Why?
quiz.a: Three. A planar free body gives only three equilibrium equations: ΣF<sub>x</sub> = 0, ΣF<sub>y</sub> = 0 and ΣM = 0.

quiz.q: Why must a section free body include the support reaction at C if C is on that part?
quiz.a: The support reaction is an external force on that part. Leaving it out gives an unbalanced free body and wrong member forces.

quiz.q: If the load at E is 14 kN downward instead of 10 kN, find CE by the same vertical section.
quiz.a: C<sub>y</sub> = 14 × 2 / 4 = 7 kN upward. ΣF<sub>y</sub> gives 7 + T<sub>CE</sub>(3/√13) = 0, so T<sub>CE</sub> = −7√13/3 = −8.41 kN. CE is 8.41 kN compression.

quiz.q: A student uses ΣM<sub>C</sub> on the right part to find CE. What does the equation actually give?
quiz.a: CE and BC both pass through C, so their moments about C are zero. The equation gives EF, and in this truss EF = 0. It does not give CE.

quiz.q: In the right free body, which way does the tension in CE act at C?
quiz.a: Toward E, up and left, in direction (−2, 3)/√13. Tension pulls away from the cut face and toward the other joint of the member.

quiz.q: Two unknown cut members meet at P. Which equilibrium equation eliminates both, and why?
quiz.a: ΣM<sub>P</sub> = 0. Both forces pass through P, so each has zero moment arm about P.

quiz.q: Can a section cut four members if one of them is a zero-force member? Explain.
quiz.a: Yes. The zero-force member has a known force, zero, so only three unknown forces remain. The three equilibrium equations can then solve them.

beyond: Not for the exam. Design offices use matrix stiffness software for large trusses, but the method of sections remains the hand check for one critical member. Influence lines for moving loads use the same cut free-body idea. Search for 'method of sections influence line', 'truss influence line', and 'zero-force members in trusses'.
